We develop a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model that captures low-energy dynamics across the insulator-to-superfluid transition. We show that commonly used cumulant expansions about the Mott ground state fail in the superfluid phase not only quantitatively but also funda…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033116] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model focusing on Berry-phase-induced canonical structure of quantum fluctuations across the Mott-superfluid transition.
motivation: To understand low-energy dynamics across the insulator-to-superfluid transition in the Bose-Hubbard model, addressing failures of cumulant expansions in the superfluid phase.
method: A unified field-theoretical approach incorporating Berry phase effects to capture quantum fluctuations across the phase transition.
result: The Berry phase induces a canonical structure that modifies the low-energy dynamics, providing a more accurate description than standard cumulant expansions.
conclusion: The Berry-phase-induced canonical structure is essential for correctly describing quantum fluctuations in the superfluid phase, offering a unified framework for the Bose-Hubbard model.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The paper presents a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and topological invariants to compute persistence diagrams more efficiently than classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over the best known classical algorithms for certain classes of topological data analysis problems.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential quantum advantage in topological data analysis, but the practical relevance depends on the availability of fault-tolerant quantum computers and the specific data sets.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent experiments recording thousands of neurons simultaneously and analyze the data using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques from statistical physics.
result: These methods uncover quantitatively reproducible behaviors in neural activity, bridging abstract theoretical principles with experimental data.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides powerful tools for understanding neural networks, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal T-count for preparing arbitrary n-qubit quantum states and implementing diagonal unitaries, achieving asymptotic scaling of O(4^n n) with ancilla qubits.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, as T gates are expensive to implement. Prior work left a gap between lower and upper bounds for state preparation.
method: The authors develop a constructive algorithm using ancilla qubits and a counting argument to prove optimality, building on techniques from Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer.
result: They show that the optimal T-count for state preparation is Θ(4^n n) with ancilla, and similarly for diagonal unitaries. They also demonstrate parallel synthesis of tensor products of single-qubit unitaries.
conclusion: The work closes the asymptotic complexity for T-count in state preparation and diagonal unitaries, providing tight bounds and practical implications for quantum circuit optimization.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting to build zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks, with applications to NP and QMA.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols are not secure against quantum verifiers that can obtain superpositions of transcripts, and previous constructions relied on commitments not known from standard assumptions.
method: The authors present a quantum generalization of the MPC-in-the-head technique, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use it to construct three-round zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA in the common reference string model, with security based on the learning with errors (LWE) assumption.
result: Two new three-round zero-knowledge protocols are obtained: one for NP and one for QMA, both secure against superposition attacks and based on LWE.
conclusion: This work provides the first zero-knowledge protocols for NP and QMA secure against superposition attacks from standard cryptographic assumptions, advancing quantum cryptography.

title: Quantum Transformer Bsde Solver Via Multi-Layer Fully-Connected Variational Quantum Circuits
authors: Howard Su, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Chi-Sheng Chen, Lance Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solving high-dimensional parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs) is important in engineering, physics, and stochastic control. Deep BSDE methods reformulate semilinear PDEs as backward stochastic differential equations and admit a model-based reinforcement learning interpretation, where trajectories are generated from known stochastic dynamics while a trainable model learns the gradient-related control process. We propose a Quantum Transformer BSDE solver based on Multi-Layer Fully-Connected Variational Quantum Circuits (FC-VQC). The method treats the normalized state trajectory as time--coordinate tokens and applies causal self-attention to learn interactions in the adapted BSDE gradient process. All trainable model parameters are contained within the FC-VQC embedding, projection, feed-forward, and decoder modules, while attention and structural operations remain classical and parameter-free. Experiments on three d=36 PDE benchmarks show that QTransformer consistently improves over the non-attentive FC-VQC baseline and outperforms the classical Transformer at compact hidden widths, while the wider classical Transformer achieves the best overall accuracy. These results demonstrate that combining causal attention with FC-VQC provides an effective quantum architecture for high-dimensional BSDE trajectory learning.
tldr: Proposes a quantum-classical hybrid solver for high-dimensional PDEs using variational quantum circuits with attention.
motivation: Solving high-dimensional parabolic PDEs is important but computationally challenging; deep BSDE methods offer a reinforcement learning approach.
method: Combines causal self-attention with multi-layer fully-connected variational quantum circuits (FC-VQC) to learn the gradient process in BSDE trajectories.
result: On d=36 PDE benchmarks, the quantum transformer outperforms non-attentive FC-VQC and classical transformer at compact widths, but wider classical transformer achieves best accuracy.
conclusion: Causal attention with FC-VQC is an effective quantum architecture for high-dimensional BSDE learning, though classical models still lead in accuracy.

title: Network Reciprocity Shapes Evolutionary Cybersecurity Dynamics
authors: Adeela Bashir, Zia Ush Shamszaman, Zhao Song, The Anh Han
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-assisted cybersecurity systems are characterised by continuous adaptation between attackers and defenders, making evolutionary game theory a natural framework for studying their long-term behaviour. However, existing evolutionary cybersecurity models have primarily focused on homogeneous interactions, providing limited understanding of how population structure influences cyber attack-defence dynamics. In this paper, we develop a mixed-role evolutionary game in which adaptive cyber agents can exhibit both offensive and defensive behaviours, and investigate its dynamics in well-mixed and structured populations. The proposed framework combines stochastic evolutionary analysis with large-scale agent-based simulations to examine how interaction structure shapes long-run strategic behaviour. Our results reveal a fundamental difference between global and local interactions. While well-mixed populations exhibit broad coexistence between attacking and defensive strategies, structured populations generate well-defined evolutionary regimes in which secure defensive behaviour becomes dominant over a much larger region of the parameter space. Spatial analysis further shows that neighbouring defenders naturally form resilient clusters that suppress persistent attacks through network reciprocity. These findings demonstrate that interaction structure is a fundamental determinant of AI-assisted cybersecurity evolution and suggest that organising defensive agents through local networked interactions can substantially improve long-term cyber resilience without requiring additional defensive incentives.
tldr: This paper uses evolutionary game theory to study how network structure influences cybersecurity dynamics between attackers and defenders.
motivation: Existing evolutionary cybersecurity models assume homogeneous interactions, ignoring the role of population structure in cyber attack-defense dynamics.
method: The authors develop a mixed-role evolutionary game model and analyze it using stochastic evolutionary analysis and agent-based simulations in both well-mixed and structured populations.
result: Structured populations lead to dominance of defensive strategies via network reciprocity, while well-mixed populations show broad coexistence.
conclusion: Interaction structure is a key determinant of cybersecurity evolution, and local networked interactions can improve long-term cyber resilience without extra incentives.

title: SignDeepSC: A Semantic Signature-based Approach For Robust Semantic Communication
authors: Khalil Alhaj, Razane Tajeddine, Hadi Sarieddeen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic communication systems such as deep semantic communication (DeepSC) offer high efficiency but are vulnerable to adversarial attacks on their underlying neural networks. We address a physical-layer man-in-the-middle (MitM) threat in which an adversary injects perturbations into the transmitted signal to distort its meaning. We propose SignDeepSC, an architectural defense that achieves adversarial robustness without requiring explicit adversarial example generation during training. The approach is built on a perceiver-inspired semantic signature, a compact vector summary of the source features transmitted over a separate low-rate auxiliary channel. This signature is used by a self-repairing decoder that leverages cross-attention to correct distortions and can additionally drive a scrambler that shuffles the feature layout. We evaluate SignDeepSC over Rayleigh fading and additive white Gaussian noise channels under both single-step fast gradient sign method (FGSM) and iterative projected gradient descent (PGD) attacks. Under PGD ([MATH]), at 12~dB signal-to-noise ratio with Rayleigh fading, SignDeepSC achieves a bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU-4) score of 0.237 and bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) sentence similarity of 0.646, outperforming all baselines without degrading clean-channel performance, when the signature channel is well protected.
tldr: This paper proposes a defense against adversarial attacks on semantic communication systems using a semantic signature and self-repairing decoder.
motivation: Semantic communication systems are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations that distort the meaning of transmitted signals, posing a security threat.
method: The approach transmits a compact semantic signature over a separate auxiliary channel, which the decoder uses via cross-attention to correct distortions, optionally with a scrambler.
result: Under PGD attacks at 12 dB SNR with Rayleigh fading, the method achieves BLEU-4 of 0.237 and BERT similarity of 0.646, outperforming baselines without degrading clean-channel performance.
conclusion: SignDeepSC provides adversarial robustness for semantic communication without requiring adversarial training, as long as the signature channel is protected.

title: The Rate-Distortion-Deception Tradeoff
authors: Semih Akkoc, Sahan Liyanaarachchi, Sennur Ulukus, Aylin Yener
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem of finding the optimal compression rate for a given random variable has been traditionally studied under two main constraints: distortion and perception. The distortion constraint enforces the fidelity of our reconstruction with respect to the observed realization of the random variable, while the perception constraint ensures that the reconstruction is close to a sample from the distribution of the random variable of interest. In this work, we explore the possibility of reconstruction, such that the reconstructed sample is still within a desired fidelity level with our original realization of the random variable, but at the same time, it resembles a sample from a different target distribution. We term this criterion as the deception constraint and find the fundamental tradeoffs of rate-distortion and deception.
tldr: This paper studies the rate-distortion-deception tradeoff, where reconstruction must be faithful to the original but resemble a different target distribution.
motivation: Traditional compression considers distortion and perception; this work introduces deception as a third constraint, motivated by applications where one wants to mislead while maintaining fidelity.
method: The authors formulate the rate-distortion-deception problem using information-theoretic rate-distortion theory and derive fundamental tradeoffs.
result: They characterize the optimal rate as a function of distortion and deception constraints, showing how deception increases the required rate.
conclusion: The work extends rate-distortion theory to include deception, providing a framework for compression with adversarial or privacy goals.

conclusion: The work contributes to understanding anyon mobility in moiré systems, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Experimental Realization Of Synthetic Magnonic Lattice Via Floquet Engineering
authors: Amin Pishehvar, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Zhaoyou Wang, Zixin Yan, Yu Jiang, Liang Jiang, Benedetta Flebus, And Xufeng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Amin Pishehvar, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Zhaoyou Wang, Zixin Yan, Yu Jiang, Liang Jiang, Benedetta Flebus, and Xufeng Zhang

Magnonic systems, which exploit spin-wave excitations in magnetic materials, offer a promising platform for coherent information processing due to their low dissipation, strong nonlinearities, and intrinsic nonreciprocity. However, scaling magnonic circuits remains challenging, particularly with low…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046706] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally realizes a synthetic magnonic lattice using Floquet engineering, demonstrating control over spin-wave dynamics.
motivation: Scaling magnonic circuits for coherent information processing is challenging; synthetic lattices offer a way to engineer complex magnonic band structures.
method: The authors use Floquet engineering with periodic driving to create a synthetic lattice in a magnonic system, and experimentally characterize the resulting band structure.
result: They successfully demonstrate the formation of a synthetic magnonic lattice and observe Floquet-induced band gaps and edge states.
conclusion: Floquet engineering provides a viable route to design magnonic circuits with tailored properties, potentially advancing magnon-based information processing.

title: Observation Of Radiation-Loss-Based Non-Hermitian Point Gap In Photonic Crystals
authors: Yuto Moritake, Nozomi Ogawa, Issei Takeda, Yusuke Ohinata, Takahiro Uemura, Taiki Yoda, Kenta Takata, Eiichi Kuramochi, Hisashi Sumikura, And Masaya Notomi
abstract:

A non-Hermitian point gap (NHPG) is a unique phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems and induces a non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). In photonic crystals, NHPG and NHSE have previously been explored mainly through material loss, where the typically low [MATH] factors make direct observation of complex freq…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046903] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of a non-Hermitian point gap in photonic crystals via radiation loss, demonstrating the non-Hermitian skin effect.
motivation: Non-Hermitian point gaps and the associated skin effect have been studied mainly with material loss; this work aims to observe them using radiation loss in photonic crystals with high Q factors.
method: The authors design photonic crystal structures with controlled radiation loss and measure the complex frequency spectra to identify the point gap and skin effect.
result: They successfully observe the non-Hermitian point gap and confirm the non-Hermitian skin effect through experimental measurements.
conclusion: Radiation loss provides a viable mechanism for realizing non-Hermitian phenomena in photonic crystals, opening new avenues for non-Hermitian photonics.

title: Flux Magnetism In A Strongly Interacting Dipolar Lattice Supersolid Under Tunable Gauge Fields
authors: Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, And Luca Barbiero
abstract:

Here we unveil a mechanism that directly connects these two regimes and can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems. Specifically, we exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthan…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flux magnetism in a dipolar lattice supersolid under tunable gauge fields, focusing on strongly correlated matter in ultracold atomic systems.
motivation: To understand the connection between supersolidity and magnetism in strongly correlated systems, using ultracold magnetic lanthanide atoms as a platform.
method: The authors theoretically model a dipolar lattice supersolid and show that tunable gauge fields induce a flux magnetism phase, characterized by chiral currents and topological order.
result: They predict a novel magnetic phase emerging from the interplay of supersolid order and gauge fields, with observable signatures in momentum-space density and noise correlations.
conclusion: This work reveals a direct mechanism linking supersolidity and magnetism, offering a new route to explore topological phases in ultracold atomic systems.

title: Hidden Dissipation In Topological Insulators: Near-field Radiation From Local Shot Noise
authors: Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, And Jian Wang
abstract:

Finite-frequency local shot noise acting as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors reveals a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy rather than conventional transport measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046303] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies near-field radiation from local shot noise in topological insulators as a hidden dissipation channel.
motivation: To identify energy-loss mechanisms in topological insulators that are not captured by conventional transport measurements.
method: The authors theoretically analyze finite-frequency local shot noise as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors.
result: They find a hidden dissipation channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected via near-field microscopy.
conclusion: Near-field radiation from shot noise provides a new way to probe dissipation in topological insulators beyond standard transport.

title: Finite-Momentum Pairing And Superlattice Superconductivity In Valley-Imbalanced Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:

Superconducting instabilities in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral tetralayer graphene reveal the formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046505] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-momentum pairing and superlattice superconductivity in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral graphene, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding superconducting instabilities in graphene systems with valley imbalance is important for condensed matter physics, but does not directly relate to the user's research interests.
method: The authors theoretically analyze superconducting instabilities in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with valley imbalance, likely using mean-field theory or similar techniques.
result: They find formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of graphene-based superconductors but lacks connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unconventional Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals: A Hyperspatial Projective Construction
authors: Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, and Huaqing Huang

Altermagnetism, a novel magnetic phase characterized by symmetry-protected, momentum-dependent spin splitting and collinear compensated magnetic moments, has thus far been explored primarily in periodic crystals. In this Letter, we extend the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals—aperiodic syst…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046704] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals using a hyperspatial projective construction.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied only in periodic crystals; this work explores its existence in aperiodic quasicrystals.
method: The authors use a hyperspatial projective construction to model altermagnetism in quasicrystals.
result: They demonstrate symmetry-protected spin splitting in quasicrystals, showing altermagnetism is not limited to periodic systems.
conclusion: Altermagnetism can occur in quasicrystals, broadening the scope of magnetic phases in aperiodic materials.

title: Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals
authors: Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, And Dong-Hui Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, and Dong-Hui Xu

Altermagnets are a recently discovered class of magnetic materials that combine a collinear, zero-magnetization spin structure, characteristic of antiferromagnets, with spin-split electronic bands, a hallmark of ferromagnets. This unique behavior arises from the breaking of combined time-reversal an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046705] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts altermagnetism in quasicrystals, a new magnetic phase combining zero net magnetization with spin-split bands.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been observed in crystals but not in quasicrystals; this work extends the concept to aperiodic systems.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model on a Penrose tiling to study the electronic structure and magnetic ordering.
result: They find that quasicrystals can host altermagnetic order with spin-split bands despite the lack of translational symmetry.
conclusion: Quasicrystals provide a new platform for altermagnetism, expanding the family of magnetic materials.

title: Magnetic Correlations In The Su(3) Triangular-Lattice $t\text{−}J$ Model At Finite Doping
authors: Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Ultracold alkaline-earth atoms and molecules now enable experimental realizations of SU(N)-symmetric Fermi-Hubbard models, yet theoretical understanding of these systems, particularly at finite doping remains limited. Here we investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations in the SU(3) triangular-lattice t-J model at finite doping using numerical methods.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models at finite doping is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical understanding is limited.
method: The authors investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard model using numerical techniques to compute magnetic correlations.
result: They find specific magnetic ordering patterns and their evolution with doping in the triangular lattice.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the magnetic properties of SU(3) systems, relevant for experiments with ultracold alkaline-earth atoms.

title: Displacive Quantum Critical Point In Superconducting Hydrides: The Case Of ${\mathrm{H}}_{3}\mathrm{S}$
authors: Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, And Michele Casula
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Cherubini, Abhishek Raghav, and Michele Casula

[MATH] sulfur hydride has been widely investigated for its high superconducting critical temperature [MATH] of 203 K at about [MATH]. Despite being the precursor of superconducting hydrides, a detailed picture of its structural phase diagra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046102] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates a displacive quantum critical point in superconducting H3S, focusing on its structural phase diagram and superconducting properties.
motivation: Understanding the structural phase diagram of H3S is crucial for explaining its high superconducting critical temperature and for designing better hydride superconductors.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and anharmonic phonon theory to map out the pressure-temperature phase diagram of H3S, identifying a quantum critical point associated with a displacive phase transition.
result: They find a displacive quantum critical point at around 140 GPa, where the superconducting critical temperature is enhanced due to soft phonon modes.
conclusion: The quantum critical point plays a key role in the high superconductivity of H3S, and similar mechanisms may be relevant for other hydride superconductors.

title: Bound States And Decay Dynamics In $N$-level Friedrichs Model With Factorizable Interactions
authors: Jia-Ming Zhang, Yu Xin, And Bing Chen

Considering an [MATH]-level system interacting factorizably with a continuous spectrum, we derive expressions for the bound states and the dynamical evolution within this single-excitation Friedrichs model by using the projection operator formalism. First, we establish explicit criteria to determine th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012214] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bound states and decay dynamics in an N-level Friedrichs model with factorizable interactions, focusing on a specific quantum optical model.
motivation: To understand the conditions for bound state formation and the dynamical evolution in a simple exactly solvable model of a discrete system coupled to a continuum.
method: Uses projection operator formalism to derive analytical expressions for bound states and time evolution in the single-excitation subspace.
result: Establishes explicit criteria for bound states and provides analytical decay dynamics.
conclusion: The work offers a complete analytical solution for the N-level Friedrichs model with factorizable interactions, which may be useful for understanding related physical systems.

title: Optical Creation Of Dark-bright Soliton Lattices In One-dimensional Multicomponent Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Y. Braver, D. Burba, Th. Busch, G. Juzeliūnas, And P. G. Kevrekidis

We present a widely accessible and experimentally realizable technique for the controlled creation of dark-bright solitons and soliton lattices in one-dimensional atomic Bose-Einstein condensates. The method is based on preparing the condensate in a dark state of a [MATH]-coupled three-level s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013319] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an optical method to create dark-bright soliton lattices in multicomponent Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: Solitons in Bose-Einstein condensates are of interest for nonlinear dynamics and matter-wave manipulation, but the paper focuses on a specific experimental technique rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose using a Λ-coupled three-level system to prepare the condensate in a dark state, which allows controlled creation of dark-bright soliton lattices.
result: The technique is shown to be experimentally realizable and produces stable soliton lattices.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for studying soliton dynamics in multicomponent condensates, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantification Of Parasitic Etalons In Fabry-Perot Cavities And The Errors They Cause In Pound-Drever-Hall Frequency Stabilization Schemes
authors: Malte Misfeldt, Emily Rose Rees, Andrew Wade, David Rabeling, And Kirk Mckenzie

Author(s): Malte Misfeldt, Emily Rose Rees, Andrew Wade, David Rabeling, and Kirk McKenzie

The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) scheme is a well-known technique for stabilizing a laser's frequency to a reference length such as an optical cavity. However, if a PDH setup is not carefully designed, one might easily create parasitic etalons, which are caused by back reflections in the optical path. Th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013521] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies parasitic etalons in Fabry-Perot cavities and their impact on Pound-Drever-Hall frequency stabilization.
motivation: Parasitic etalons can degrade the performance of PDH frequency stabilization, but their effects are not well characterized.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model and experimental setup to measure etalon-induced errors in PDH error signals.
result: They quantify the magnitude of frequency errors caused by parasitic etalons and propose mitigation strategies.
conclusion: Careful design is needed to avoid parasitic etalons in PDH setups; the work provides guidelines for improving frequency stability.

title: Tuning Density And Spin Ordering Of Degenerate Fermi Gases In An Optical Cavity
authors: Wei Qin, Yuan-Hong Chen, And Renyuan Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Qin, Yuan-Hong Chen, and Renyuan Liao

The authors present the thermodynamic phase diagram for a degenerate Fermi gas in a high‑finesse cavity, where the competition between scalar‑vectorial interactions and Pauli exclusion governs the phase structure. They find that the phase transition threshold is determined by the scalar-vectorial coupling weight and Pauli blocking, with the latter dictating the critical pump lattice depth required for the onset of superradiance.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L011302] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamic phase diagram of a degenerate Fermi gas in an optical cavity, focusing on density and spin ordering.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between scalar-vectorial interactions and Pauli exclusion in cavity-coupled Fermi gases.
method: The authors derive the thermodynamic phase diagram by analyzing the competition between interactions and Pauli blocking.
result: The phase transition threshold is determined by scalar-vectorial coupling weight and Pauli blocking, which dictates the critical pump lattice depth for superradiance.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase structure of degenerate Fermi gases in cavities, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

title: Continuous-time Quantum Walks On A Defective Lattice: Boosting The Spreading Of Delocalized States Through Parrondo's Strategy
authors: João V. Cordeiro, Eduardo I. Duzzioni, And Edgard P. M. Amorim

The defect is modeled by assigning complex-valued hopping amplitudes to the edges that connect the site corresponding to the mean position of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012459] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies continuous-time quantum walks on a defective lattice and uses Parrondo's strategy to boost spreading of delocalized states.
motivation: Understanding quantum transport in disordered systems is important for quantum information processing, but the paper focuses on a specific transport phenomenon rather than core quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional lattice with a single defect using complex hopping amplitudes and apply Parrondo's strategy to enhance delocalization.
result: They find that the spreading of delocalized states can be significantly boosted by alternating between two different defective configurations.
conclusion: Parrondo's strategy can be effectively used to improve quantum transport in defective lattices, which may have implications for quantum walks and related applications.

title: Limitations Of Entangled Two-photon Absorption Detection
authors: R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, And B. Brecht
abstract:
Author(s): R. Pollmann, F. Roeder, C. Silberhorn, and B. Brecht

We introduce a method for determining the sensitivity of any given entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) measurement. motivation: Entangled two-photon absorption (ETPA) is a promising technique for spectroscopy and sensing, but its practical sensitivity is limited by noise and background. Understanding these limitations is crucial for designing effective ETPA experiments.
method: The authors model all signal and noise contributions to an ETPA measurement and derive a single numerical value (in Göppert-Mayer units) that characterizes the measurement sensitivity.
result: They identify fundamental and practical limitations on ETPA detection sensitivity, showing that noise sources such as linear absorption and detector dark counts impose bounds on achievable sensitivity.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for evaluating ETPA measurement setups and highlights the challenges that must be overcome for practical applications.

title: Origins Of The Intrinsic Noise Of Zero-field Metastable Helium-4 Optically Pumped Magnetometers
authors: Alexandre Stathopulos, Rudy Romain, Sergey Mitryukovskiy, And Agustin Palacios-Laloy

motivation: Understanding noise origins is crucial for improving sensitivity of optically pumped magnetometers used in magnetic field sensing.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive experimental characterization of a single-beam vector magnetometer, identifying and quantifying noise contributions from various sources.
result: The sensor achieves vector magnetic readings with noise below 300 fT/√Hz in its optimal regime, and the main noise origins are identified.
conclusion: The study provides a detailed noise budget for zero-field helium-4 magnetometers, guiding future sensor optimization.

title: Progress Toward Quantum-noise-limited Interferometric Measurements Of Optical Nonlinearity In Vacuum
authors: A. Aras, A. E. Kraych, X. Sarazin, E. Baynard, F. Couchot, And M. Pittman

Quantum electrodynamics predicts that the vacuum must behave as a nonlinear optical medium: The vacuum optical index should increase when it is stressed by intense electromagnetic fields. The Deflection of Light by Light project aims to measure it by using intense and ultrashort laser pulses. The ex…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013519] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports progress toward measuring the quantum-noise-limited optical nonlinearity of vacuum, a test of quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: Quantum electrodynamics predicts that vacuum behaves as a nonlinear optical medium under intense fields; measuring this effect tests fundamental physics.
method: The experiment uses intense ultrashort laser pulses in an interferometric setup to detect the deflection of light by light, aiming for quantum-noise-limited sensitivity.
result: The paper describes progress in achieving the required sensitivity, but does not report a definitive measurement of vacuum nonlinearity.
conclusion: Further improvements are needed to reach the quantum-noise limit and confirm the predicted nonlinearity.

motivation: Understanding the interplay between gauge fields and disorder in mesoscopic systems is important for quantum transport, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive the disorder-averaged density matrix using weak-localization theory and analyze time- and momentum-resolved dynamics.
result: They find that uniform SU(2) gauge fields modify spin-momentum relaxation and coherent backscattering signatures.
conclusion: The results provide insights into mesoscopic scattering under gauge fields, but do not directly contribute to quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Percolation-driven Ferromagnetism In A Dilute Magnetic Topological Insulator
authors: Farhan Islam, Santanu Pakhira, Deborah L. Schlagel, Dhurba R. Jaishi, Daniel M. Pajerowski, Thomas Heitmann, David C. Johnston, Robert J. Mcqueeney, And David Vaknin

motivation: To understand the emergence of long-range ferromagnetic order in a dilute magnetic topological insulator, which is relevant for spintronics and topological quantum computing.
method: Single-crystal neutron scattering and magnetic susceptibility measurements on (Sb1-xCrx)2Te3.
result: Long-range ferromagnetic order emerges below Tc=12 K, driven by percolation of magnetic clusters.
conclusion: The ferromagnetism in this dilute magnetic topological insulator is percolation-driven, providing insight into magnetic order in topological insulators.

title: Superconductivity Near A Quantum Critical Point: Bounds On The Transition Temperature In The $γ$-model
authors: Ahmed Elezaby And Artem Abanov

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024512] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superconductivity near a quantum critical point in a metal, focusing on bounds for the transition temperature in the γ-model.
motivation: Understanding how strong fermion-fermion interactions mediated by soft bosons near a quantum critical point affect non-Fermi liquid behavior and unconventional superconductivity.
method: The authors analyze the γ-model, likely using analytical methods to derive bounds on the superconducting transition temperature.
result: Bounds on the transition temperature are obtained, showing deviations from conventional BCS and Migdal-Eliashberg theories.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical constraints on superconductivity near quantum critical points, relevant to condensed matter physics but not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Superconducting Diode Effect In The Weak Localization Regime
authors: Naratip Nunchot And Youichi Yanase
abstract:

We study a dirty two-dimensional superconductor with Rashba spin–orbit coupling and in-plane Zeeman fields described by the nonlinear sigma model that includes the Cooper and long-range Coulomb interactions. The renormalized Ginzburg–Landau theory, which includes the weak localization effects at the…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024513] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the superconducting diode effect in a dirty two-dimensional superconductor with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and in-plane Zeeman fields, focusing on weak localization effects.
motivation: The superconducting diode effect is a phenomenon where the critical current depends on the direction, which has potential applications in superconducting electronics. Understanding its origin in disordered systems is important.
method: The authors use a nonlinear sigma model that includes Cooper and long-range Coulomb interactions, and develop a renormalized Ginzburg-Landau theory incorporating weak localization effects.
result: They find that weak localization corrections can induce a superconducting diode effect, and analyze its dependence on disorder strength and other parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical understanding of the superconducting diode effect in the weak localization regime, highlighting the role of quantum corrections.

title: Quantum Decay Of Magnons In The Unfrustrated Honeycomb Heisenberg Model
authors: Calvin Krämer, Dag-Björn Hering, Vanessa Sulaiman, Matthias R. Walther, Götz S. Uhrig, And Kai Phillip Schmidt

We investigate the physical properties of elementary magnon excitations of the ordered antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice using quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations, series expansions (SE), and continuous similarity transformations (CST). The stochastic analytic continuatio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034424] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon decay in the honeycomb Heisenberg antiferromagnet using QMC, SE, and CST methods.
motivation: Understanding magnon lifetimes and decay mechanisms in quantum antiferromagnets is important for interpreting neutron scattering experiments.

title: Localization Phase Diagram Of The Hexagonal Lattice With Irrational Magnetic Flux

tldr: This paper studies the localization phase diagram of the Hofstadter model on a hexagonal lattice with irrational magnetic flux.

title: Electron Hydrodynamics And Bernoulli Effect In Venturi-shaped Two-dimensional Systems
authors: C. A. Monari, A. D. Levin, A. S. Jaroshevich, Z. D. Kvon, V. A. Chitta, D. V. Dmitriev, A. K. Bakarov, And G. M. Gusev

motivation: To demonstrate strongly nonlinear transport regimes in electron hydrodynamics beyond the linear response regime.

motivation: Understanding frustration and disorder in complex systems is central to statistical physics and quantum annealing.
method: The authors develop a bond-correlated percolation model to analyze relaxation dynamics in spin glasses on complex networks.
result: They find that the percolation approach captures key features of the dynamics, including scaling behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how topology affects spin glass relaxation, relevant for quantum annealing hardware.

title: Nonperturbative Effects Of Short-range Spatial Correlations At The Two-particle Level
authors: Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, And Alessandro Toschi
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, and Alessandro Toschi

By means of cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT), we study how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of the self-consistent perturbation theory in two-dimensional systems and the most relevant physical consequences associated with it, such as the CDMFT Mott transition. To this aim, we…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033093] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonperturbative effects of short-range spatial correlations in two-dimensional systems using cellular dynamical mean-field theory, focusing on the Mott transition.
motivation: To understand how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of self-consistent perturbation theory and the resulting physical consequences like the Mott transition.
method: Cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) is employed to analyze short-range correlations in two-dimensional systems.
result: The study identifies nonperturbative effects due to short-range correlations and their role in the CDMFT Mott transition.
conclusion: Short-range spatial correlations have significant nonperturbative effects on the Mott transition in two-dimensional systems.

title: Orbital Hall Effect From Orbital Magnetic Moments Of Bloch States: The Role Of A New Correction Term
authors: Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:
Author(s): Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, and Tatiana G. Rappoport

We present a rigorous derivation of the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) of Bloch states. Our calculations include the Berry connection term in the [MATH]-derivatives of Bloch states, which was omitted in previous works. The resulting formula for the OMM matrix elements applies to a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033086] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a correction term for the orbital magnetic moment of Bloch states and applies it to compute the intrinsic orbital Hall effect in metals.
motivation: Previous calculations of the orbital magnetic moment omitted a Berry connection term; this work aims to provide a rigorous derivation and assess its impact on the orbital Hall effect.
method: The authors derive the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment including the Berry connection term, and compute the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity for several metals using first-principles methods.
result: The correction term significantly affects the orbital Hall conductivity in certain materials, leading to improved agreement with experimental observations.
conclusion: Including the Berry connection term is essential for accurate predictions of the orbital Hall effect, and the corrected formalism should be adopted in future studies.

title: Twist-driven Interlayer Hybridization And Multiple Mobility Edges In Bilayer Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong

We investigate two coupled one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper rings with [MATH] sites, where a site-dependent angular twist in the second ring generates a spatially varying mosaic of distance-modulated couplings. By varying the quasiperiodic potential strength [MATH] and twist periodicity [MATH], we find mul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033079] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mobility edges in bilayer quasiperiodic lattices with twist-induced interlayer hybridization.
motivation: Understanding localization phenomena in quasiperiodic systems is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors investigate two coupled Aubry-André-Harper rings with a site-dependent angular twist, analyzing the quasiperiodic potential strength and twist periodicity.
result: They find multiple mobility edges and interlayer hybridization effects.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of quasiperiodic lattices but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the extended SSH model.
motivation: Understanding topology at finite temperature is important for realistic systems, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors compare three diagnostics: ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and a many-body invariant, applied to the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension.
result: The ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined at nonzero temperature and captures topological transitions, while the other diagnostics show limitations.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a robust indicator of topology at finite temperature for non-interacting systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Population Model With Square-root Growth Noise And Cell-size Regulation
authors: Farshid Jafarpour
abstract:
Author(s): Farshid Jafarpour

Stochastic exponential growth is nearly ubiquitous across cellular life, but how its microscopic noise structure shapes population growth remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce an exactly solvable population model in which cells grow exponentially with fluctuations that scale with the square …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033082] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: An exactly solvable stochastic population model with square-root growth noise and cell-size regulation is introduced and analyzed.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic noise structure affects population growth in cellular systems is poorly understood, motivating the development of a tractable model.
method: The authors propose a stochastic model where cells grow exponentially with fluctuations scaling as the square root of cell size, and solve it exactly using analytical techniques.
result: Exact solutions for population statistics are obtained, revealing how noise and cell-size regulation shape growth dynamics.
conclusion: The model provides a framework for studying stochastic exponential growth in cellular populations, with implications for understanding noise in biological systems.

title: Statistical Physics Of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning Of A Multilayer Perceptron Near Interpolation
authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, and Rudy Skerk

Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031014] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical physics and random matrix theory to analyze generalization in deep neural networks near interpolation.
motivation: Understanding generalization in deep learning is a central challenge; the authors aim to derive exact generalization error for a multilayer perceptron.
method: They apply tools from statistical physics (replica method, cavity method) and random matrix theory to a deep fully connected network with random features.
result: They derive the generalization error and show how feature learning propagates across layers, revealing mechanisms governing behavior near the interpolation threshold.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical characterization of deep learning generalization using physics-inspired methods, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Engineered Molecular Clock Transitions For Precision Measurements
authors: Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, And Nicholas R. Hutzler
abstract:
Author(s): Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, and Nicholas R. Hutzler

Special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules have been engineered to probe physics beyond the standard model, suppressing disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031011] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates engineered molecular clock transitions in heavy polar molecules for precision measurements to probe physics beyond the standard model.
motivation: To suppress electromagnetic noise in molecular clocks while maintaining high sensitivity for fundamental physics tests.
method: Engineering special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules that are insensitive to external electromagnetic fields.
result: Achieved suppression of disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.
conclusion: Engineered molecular clock transitions enable high-precision measurements for probing new physics beyond the standard model.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, and Cristian Cassella

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Ising machines based on parametric oscillators often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems. The authors aim to improve solution accuracy by introducing Floquet amplitude modulations.
method: The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations into the parametric oscillator network to help the system escape local minima during the optimization process.
result: The Floquet-based approach significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator-based Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet amplitude modulations are an effective technique to enhance the performance of Ising machines for combinatorial optimization.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayers.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a novel phase of matter combining topology and strong correlations, but experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy is used to measure the out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response of a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: The observed antiferromagnetic response provides evidence for a putative fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings suggest twisted MoTe2 is a promising platform for realizing fractional topological insulators.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: A mathematical framework for coupling quantum fields to classical spacetime using covariant path integrals.
motivation: To reconcile quantum mechanics with general relativity by allowing quantum matter to backreact on a classical spacetime.
method: Develops a covariant path integral formalism that treats spacetime as classical while matter remains quantum, incorporating stochastic dynamics.
result: Provides a consistent mathematical framework for backreaction, with potential experimental tests.
conclusion: The framework offers a way to test whether spacetime is fundamentally classical or quantum.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery in physics by exploring and modeling physical systems.
motivation: To accelerate scientific discovery by using large language models to autonomously explore and model physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large language model, which iteratively proposes experiments, analyzes data, and refines models.
result: The agent successfully uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems, demonstrating automated scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate parts of the scientific research process, potentially accelerating discovery in physics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation far below the mode coupling temperature.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are performed at temperatures significantly below the mode coupling temperature to analyze particle dynamics.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism for structural relaxation in this regime.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems at deep supercooling.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experimental demonstrations.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage demonstrations operate in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, so a theoretical foundation for the saturated regime is needed.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic arguments and hardness proofs tailored to BosonSampling with a linear number of modes, analyzing the computational complexity of sampling from the output distribution.
result: They prove that BosonSampling in the saturated regime remains hard for classical computers under plausible conjectures, extending the theoretical basis to match experimental conditions.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for photonic quantum advantage experiments, confirming that they are classically hard even with linear mode counts.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To develop a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons and understand their role as low-energy excitations in ferromagnetic spin chains.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their dynamics and condensation.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The framework enables detection of these solitons via inelastic neutron scattering, providing a new perspective on soliton dynamics in quantum spin systems.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of 3D fermionic CFTs and explore emergent supersymmetry using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs, computing spectra and correlation functions.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and provide evidence for a conformal fixed point.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere is a powerful tool for studying 3D fermionic CFTs, and emergent supersymmetry may be a generic feature of such theories.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.

result: The framework successfully infers causal links across a range of networked dynamics.
conclusion: The method provides a general tool for link prediction in complex networks.

authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian

authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi

authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.

authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix

motivation: Quantum linear system solvers are fundamental for many applications, but the field lacks a unified review of algorithmic techniques.
