LEAKFORGE samples this family to synthesize large-scale, device-diverse accelerometer traces from ordinary speech, explicitly modeling electromechanical transfer, structural resonances, filtering, and aliasing. An eavesdropping model trained entirely in this synthetic domain can then be applied directly to traces from previously unseen smartphones.
tldr: A framework for acoustic eavesdropping via smartphone accelerometers using physics-guided data generation.
motivation: To enable cross-device accelerometer-based speech eavesdropping without requiring per-device training data.
method: Models the audio-to-accelerometer transfer function family and synthesizes large-scale training data from ordinary speech.
result: The eavesdropping model trained on synthetic data works on previously unseen smartphones.
conclusion: Device-specific leakage can be parameterized and exploited for practical eavesdropping.

title: Architectural Backdoors In Vision-Language Model Supply Chains Via Representation Steering
authors: Maria Rosaria Briglia, Igor Maljkovic, Antonio Emanuele Cin\`a, Luca Oneto, Iacopo Masi, Fabio Roli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision--Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed through a model supply chain in which pretrained checkpoints, architecture definitions, text encoders, and exported computation graphs are distributed by third parties and reused across downstream services. This reuse model creates a security-critical trust boundary: VLM deployments inherit not only learned parameters but also executable behavior encoded in shared model artifacts. In this paper, we show that a malicious provider can exploit this trust boundary by embedding architectural backdoors into VLM supply chains through representation steering. Our attack introduces dormant steering logic into the model architecture through a trigger-gated additive modification of an intermediate representation, without poisoning training data, controlling downstream fine-tuning, or modifying prompts at deployment time. When the trigger is absent, the modification reduces to zero and the model follows its normal computation, preserving clean utility. When the trigger is present, a steering direction shifts the internal representation toward an attacker-defined objective. We evaluate the attack across multiple VLM families and downstream tasks, including visual question answering, text-to-image generation, retrieval, and semantic response biasing. The results show that the proposed architectural steering backdoor compromises integrity, safety enforcement, and ranking fairness while preserving normal behavior on clean inputs. We further show that shared VLM artifacts can carry dormant steering logic against downstream services, and we propose an auditing defense that inspects the executable logic distributed with model artifacts rather than only their learned weights.
tldr: This paper introduces architectural backdoors in vision-language model supply chains via representation steering, a security attack that does not involve quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses security vulnerabilities in VLM supply chains where third-party artifacts can embed malicious behavior.
method: The attack adds trigger-gated steering logic to intermediate representations, remaining dormant without the trigger and shifting representations toward an attacker-defined objective when triggered.
result: The attack compromises integrity, safety, and fairness across multiple VLM tasks while preserving normal behavior on clean inputs.
conclusion: The work highlights the need for auditing defenses that inspect executable logic in model artifacts, not just learned weights.

title: Optimistic Verifiable Claims: A Blockchain Protocol For Conditionally Confidential Bidding In Decentralized Manufacturing
authors: Marko Corn, Nejc Ro\v{z}man, Primo\v{z} Podr\v{z}aj
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decentralized manufacturing faces a pre-contractual impasse: a Provider cannot price a service accurately without inspecting the design file, yet the Consumer cannot share that file without exposing intellectual property. We introduce the Optimistic Verifiable Claim (OVC), a blockchain protocol that lets a Consumer publish a verifiable claim about a concealed design (such as the material it consumes) and a Provider price and bid on it without seeing the design. The claim is committed when the service is posted and stands unless the selected Provider challenges it; a challenge triggers a deterministic on-chain check that exposes any dishonesty, and the design is disclosed only to settle a dispute, never on the honest path. We implement four checks (authorized key access, delivery-channel integrity, syntactic conformance, and declared material consumption) in Solidity and measure them on a real 6.41 MB G-code file, the 3DBenchy, across Ethereum, Arbitrum, and opBNB. Every service incurs the cost of posting the encrypted design, with or without a dispute. For the 3DBenchy, the no-dispute outcome costs \[MATH]288 in 3 min on Arbitrum, and \[MATH]49,660 in up to 57 hours on Ethereum, \[MATH]19.73 in 13 min on opBNB. Costs and times grow with size: for a 50 MB industrial design, an undisputed service reaches \[MATH]22.36 and 16 min on opBNB, and a fully contested dispute reaches \[MATH]195 and 1.6 hours on opBNB. Of the four, the material-consumption check is the costliest, its predicate being the most expensive to evaluate on-chain. OVC makes confidential, claim-based bidding economically feasible on Arbitrum and opBNB, but not on Ethereum at industrial scale.
tldr: This paper proposes a blockchain protocol for confidential bidding in decentralized manufacturing, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Decentralized manufacturing faces a pre-contractual impasse where providers need design information to price services, but consumers want to protect intellectual property.
method: The Optimistic Verifiable Claim (OVC) protocol allows consumers to publish verifiable claims about concealed designs, with on-chain checks triggered only if a provider challenges the claim.
result: The protocol is implemented and tested on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and opBNB, showing economic feasibility on Arbitrum and opBNB but not on Ethereum for industrial-scale designs.
conclusion: OVC enables confidential, claim-based bidding in decentralized manufacturing, but scalability and cost remain challenges on certain blockchains.

title: Kemeny Rank Aggregation Is NP-Hard For Three Voters
authors: Dominik Peters
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rank aggregation is the task of combining [MATH] input rankings (linear orders) of alternatives into a single output ranking. The Kemeny rank aggregation rule selects the output ranking that minimizes the total Kendall-tau distance to the input rankings, i.e., the total number of adjacent swaps that need to be performed across input rankings so that they are all equal to the output ranking. Dwork et al. (2001) proved that the problem of computing such a ranking is NP-complete for every even [MATH] and asked whether hardness holds even for [MATH]. We give a hardness reduction from MAX CUT that proves the problem is NP-complete for [MATH]. The reduction was found in July 2026 by GPT 5.6 Sol Ultra and simplified in part with help from Claude Fable 5.
tldr: This paper proves that Kemeny rank aggregation is NP-hard for three voters, using a reduction from MAX CUT.
motivation: The computational complexity of Kemeny rank aggregation was known to be NP-complete for even numbers of voters, but the case of three voters remained open. Resolving this question completes the complexity classification.
method: The authors construct a reduction from the MAX CUT problem to Kemeny rank aggregation with three voters, showing that finding an optimal ranking is NP-hard.
result: Kemeny rank aggregation is NP-complete for three voters, closing the open problem posed by Dwork et al. (2001).
conclusion: The problem is NP-complete for all numbers of voters except possibly one or two, where it is polynomial-time solvable.

title: Mapping CVEs To Mitre Att&ck Techniques: A Curated Gold-Set Classifier And The Limits Of LLM-Assisted Label Expansion
authors: Alexandre Dulaunoy C\'edric Bonhomme
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a reproducible pipeline for mapping Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) to MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise techniques from free-text vulnerability descriptions. Rather than relying on the CWE->CAPEC->ATT&CK derivation chain, whose table-expansion artifacts we quantify, we train a multi-label classifier on a curated gold dataset of 1,207 CVEs from expert MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense mappings. The resulting model approximately doubles recall@5 compared with a zero-shot embedding-similarity baseline and improves every ranking metric. We then investigate whether LLM-assisted labeling can extend the gold dataset. Initial experiments suggest contradictory conclusions: a single run indicates degraded performance, while averaging over five random seeds suggests a small gain. However, an independent replication and an expansion-size study (100--984 additional CVEs) show that the apparent improvement is an evaluation artifact. LLM-generated labels, with approximately 0.39 agreement with expert annotations, provide no reliable improvement at any expansion size and reduce rare-technique coverage at around 1,000 added CVEs (macro-F1 decreases by 0.04). The root cause is evaluation noise. Selecting checkpoints on a small test split effectively maximizes over many noisy evaluations, producing recall@5 differences of up to 0.05 between otherwise identical runs. Using a corrected protocol based on validation-split checkpoint selection, the gold-only model achieves recall@5 of (0.673 \pm 0.019), and repeating the decisive experiment confirms the null result for LLM expansion. A final scaling study shows that additional expert-curated data consistently improves performance, whereas LLM-labeled data does not, indicating that the classifier is limited by label quality rather than dataset size. All datasets, models, code, and training logs are publicly released.
tldr: This paper presents a pipeline for mapping CVEs to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, focusing on cybersecurity threat intelligence, not quantum information theory.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the mapping of vulnerability descriptions to attack techniques, addressing limitations of existing derivation chains and evaluating the utility of LLM-assisted labeling.
method: They train a multi-label classifier on a curated gold dataset of 1,207 CVEs and test LLM-assisted label expansion, using validation-split checkpoint selection to avoid evaluation noise.
result: The gold-only model achieves recall@5 of 0.673, while LLM-generated labels provide no reliable improvement and reduce rare-technique coverage.
conclusion: Additional expert-curated data improves performance, but LLM-labeled data does not, indicating label quality is the limiting factor.

title: Kernel-Checked Exclusions For The Erd\H{o}s-Selfridge Odd Covering Problem: Any Odd Covering Of $\mathbb{Z}$ Has Lcm Exceeding 10000
authors: Shayaan Siddique Ibrahim Mian
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Erds-Selfridge odd covering problem (Erds problem #7) asks whether a covering system of [MATH] exists whose moduli are all odd, distinct, and greater than 1. The problem is open. We present a Lean 4 formalization, checked end to end by the proof kernel, of the exclusion: any covering of [MATH] by finitely many congruence classes with distinct odd moduli > 1 has lcm of the moduli exceeding 10000. The proof composes a formalized density argument (a covering by divisors of [MATH] exceeding 1 forces [MATH], so the lcm is abundant or perfect), a kernel-checked abundancy floor (no odd [MATH] qualifies), a family of Chinese-Remainder capacity certificates -- decidable per-[MATH] arithmetic inequalities each refuting every covering with distinct moduli > 1 dividing that [MATH] -- for all 23 odd abundant numbers below [MATH], and a kernel-checked enumeration establishing that those 23 are the only odd non-deficient candidates. The result is transported to the official StrictCoveringSystem [MATH] formulation of Erds #7 in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, with a bidirectional periodicity bridge between coverings of [MATH] and finite checks over [MATH] suitable for consuming future SAT-style search output. All 63 published theorems depend on exactly propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound: no sorry, no native_decide, no solver in the trusted base. The mathematical content is known -- the density argument is folklore, and far larger uncertified classifications of covering numbers exist -- so the contribution is epistemic rather than mathematical: these exclusions are theorems of the Lean kernel, with an axiom gate enforced mechanically in continuous integration.
tldr: This paper formalizes a known mathematical exclusion for the Erdős–Selfridge odd covering problem using the Lean 4 proof assistant, but does not contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The Erdős–Selfridge odd covering problem is a long-standing open problem in number theory; the authors aim to provide a fully kernel-checked proof that any odd covering of integers must have lcm exceeding 10000.
method: The proof uses a density argument, abundancy floor checks, Chinese-Remainder capacity certificates for 23 odd abundant numbers, and a bidirectional periodicity bridge, all formalized in Lean 4 with minimal axioms.
result: The formalization proves that any covering of ℤ by finitely many congruence classes with distinct odd moduli >1 has lcm > 10000, and the proof is verified by the Lean kernel.
conclusion: The contribution is epistemic (formal verification) rather than mathematical, and has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information theory.

title: Universal Individual-Sequence Prediction With A Primitive-Recursive Superpredictor
authors: Amir Leshem
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sequential prediction of individual binary sequences under zero-one loss. No computable master can compete on every sequence with all total computable predictors. We therefore consider rational-valued primitive-recursive forecasters, a broad syntactically enumerable class containing finite-state, context-based, and Prediction by Partial Matching (PPM) rules. We construct a computable probabilistic predictor with an explicit sublinear regret bound relative to every primitive-recursive forecaster on every individual sequence. We further prove that the PPM predictor is primitive recursive. Consequently, our predictor attains the infinite-past Bayes error on every Martin-L\"of random realization of every computable stationary ergodic binary source. This optimality extends to finitely many independent such sources interleaved according to an arbitrary primitive-recursive schedule. Finally, we establish strict separations from finite-state prediction and from every fixed primitive-recursive predictor. keywords: Universal prediction, individual sequences, prediction with expert advice, primitive recursive functions, Kolmogorov complexity, PPM.
tldr: This paper studies universal sequential prediction of individual binary sequences using primitive-recursive forecasters, achieving sublinear regret bounds.
motivation: To construct a computable predictor that can compete with all primitive-recursive forecasters on every individual sequence, addressing limitations of computable masters.
method: The paper constructs a probabilistic predictor with explicit sublinear regret bounds relative to any primitive-recursive forecaster, and proves that the PPM predictor is primitive recursive.
result: The predictor attains the infinite-past Bayes error on every Martin-Löf random realization of any computable stationary ergodic binary source, and extends to interleaved sources.
conclusion: The work establishes strict separations from finite-state prediction and fixed primitive-recursive predictors, demonstrating the power of primitive-recursive forecasters.

title: Algorithms For Candidate Control In Greedy Participatory Budgeting Rules
authors: Krzysztof Sornat \v{s}imon Schierreich
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of candidate control in participatory budgeting elections. Our focus is on two prominent sequential welfare-based rules---GreedyAV and GreedyCost---which are widely used in practice. Candidate control asks whether we can strategically modify the set of available candidates so as to either ensure that a preferred candidate [MATH] is selected or prevent [MATH] from being selected. Since all variants of candidate control under the two rules we consider are known to be NP-hard, we analyze the problems through the lens of parameterized complexity and approximability. Under the first lens, we provide a comprehensive classification with respect to natural parameters such as the number of voters, the number of controlled candidates, and the number of distinct costs, as well as their combinations. Within the second perspective, we establish a tight approximability bound.
tldr: This paper studies candidate control in participatory budgeting elections using greedy welfare-based rules.
motivation: To understand the computational complexity of strategic candidate manipulation in participatory budgeting.
method: Parameterized complexity analysis and approximability bounds for candidate control problems under GreedyAV and GreedyCost rules.
result: Comprehensive classification of parameterized complexity and tight approximability bounds for the problems.
conclusion: The problems remain hard under various parameterizations, but some fixed-parameter tractable cases exist.

title: A Structuration Approach To Theorizing Cybersecurity Practice: The Starc Model
authors: Md Aktaruzzaman, Atif Ahmad, Sean Maynard
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem: Cybersecurity practice runs simultaneously across analysts, teams, organizations, sectors, and regulators, co-evolves with adversaries, and increasingly blends human and algorithmic decision-making. The theories applied to it operate at single organizational levels and cannot explain why organizations with broadly similar controls differ sharply in resilience. This paper: We develop STARC (Structuration Theory Adaptation for Resilient Cybersecurity), a framework for locating where cybersecurity practice succeeds or fails structurally. It extends Giddens' Structuration Theory with three innovations, Multi-Level Adversarial Agency, Threat-Adaptive Structuration, and Material-Agential Structural Properties, across five structure-agency triads. Evidence base: STARC is illustrated through re-analysis of three financial organizations, an Australian, an Indonesian, and a Malaysian bank, across 20 interviews from SOC analysts to senior executives, selected as diverse insourced and outsourced configurations rather than as a comparison of equivalents. Cybersecurity contribution: STARC offers a structural account of why differently resourced and outsourced organizations differ in resilience, and a vocabulary for diagnosing incident-response breakdown across levels, tempos, and the human-algorithm authority boundary that single-level frameworks leave invisible. Theory and outputs: It extends Structuration Theory to adversarial, multi-level, and hybrid human-algorithmic contexts, and yields seven testable propositions linking structuration to resilience, offered for future testing.
tldr: This paper develops a structuration theory framework for cybersecurity practice, unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Existing cybersecurity theories operate at single organizational levels and fail to explain differences in resilience across organizations.
method: The authors extend Giddens' Structuration Theory with three innovations and illustrate the framework through re-analysis of interviews from three banks.
result: The STARC framework provides a structural account of resilience differences and yields seven testable propositions.
conclusion: STARC offers a vocabulary for diagnosing incident-response breakdowns across levels and human-algorithm boundaries.

title: Verification Of Provers And Solvers
authors: Ren\'e Thiemann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic deduction tools such as automatic theorem provers, SAT (satisfiability) solvers, SMT (satisfiability modulo theories) solvers, and termination analyzers can be connected to proof assistants using various approaches, notably by certification and verification. This chapter reviews and compares the approaches available, and mentions several successful applications.
tldr: This paper reviews approaches for connecting automatic deduction tools to proof assistants via certification and verification.
motivation: To compare and contrast certification and verification methods for integrating automatic theorem provers, SAT/SMT solvers, and termination analyzers with proof assistants.
method: The chapter reviews existing approaches, categorizing them into certification and verification, and discusses several successful applications.
result: The paper provides a comparative analysis of the two approaches, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses.
conclusion: Certification and verification are both viable strategies, with the choice depending on the specific tool and proof assistant context.

title: From Role Prompt To Infinite Thinking: Exploiting Persona Conditioning For Inference Cost Attacks In LLMs
authors: Zhiyi Mou, Wangze Ni, Tianfang Xiao, Haoyang LI, Chen Jason Zhang, Hanzhi Ma, Yang Bai, Zhibo Wang, Kui Ren
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, making inference efficiency and service reliability critical concerns due to their substantial computational costs. However, the autoregressive generation mechanism of LLMs enables malicious prompts to manipulate generation behaviors, inducing excessive token generation that amplifies computational consumption and threatens service efficiency. Existing methods mainly rely on adversarial suffixes or explicit extension instructions, which introduce detectable behaviors and limit their applicability. In this paper, we reveal a previously unexplored vulnerability caused by persona consistency in LLMs, where models maintain assigned roles and reproduce corresponding behaviors even when they result in inefficient reasoning and excessive generation. Based on this observation, we propose RolePlay, a task-aware dynamic persona alignment framework that constructs adaptive personas to naturally induce inefficient yet semantically coherent behaviors for inference cost amplification. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and diverse task datasets demonstrate that RolePlay consistently outperforms existing inference extension methods, achieving an average token amplification of up to and a maximum token amplification ratio of . Our findings identify persona conditioning as a new attack surface for LLM inference efficiency and offer a new perspective on computational cost amplification.
tldr: This paper identifies a vulnerability in LLMs where persona conditioning can be exploited to induce excessive token generation, increasing inference costs.
motivation: LLM inference is computationally expensive, and existing attack methods are detectable; the authors aim to reveal a new attack surface via persona consistency.
method: They propose RolePlay, a task-aware dynamic persona alignment framework that constructs adaptive personas to naturally induce inefficient yet coherent generation.
result: RolePlay achieves significant token amplification, outperforming existing inference extension methods across multiple LLMs and tasks.
conclusion: Persona conditioning is a new attack surface for LLM inference efficiency, highlighting the need for defenses against such computational cost amplification attacks.

title: Effort Matters In Score-Based Admissions: How Retaking And Aggregation Shape Test Scores
authors: Christine Ling, Diptangshu Sen, Juba Ziani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Observed standardized test scores are the result of an endogenous process: students strategically allocate effort across multiple retake attempts to improve their outcomes. Because students differ in their ability to make these investments, the interaction between applicant strategy and institutional scoring rules---such as the widely used Single-Sitting and Superscoring policies---can disparately distort observed scores. We develop a strategic framework where students allocate effort in response to different scoring policies. We show that Superscoring---the practice of combining the best section scores across attempts---introduces systematic score inflation through order-statistic selection over noise draws. This degrades signal accuracy and amplifies wealth-based disparities by disproportionately rewarding applicants who can afford repeated testing. Conversely, Single-Sitting---which keeps the best overall score rather than section-level scores---preserves signal fidelity but excludes high-ability students who lack the resources to prepare for all subjects simultaneously. Neither rule uniformly dominates; instead, they force a structural trade-off between statistical precision and fair outcomes. Finally, to address this, we propose three algorithmic interventions which either modify how scores from multiple attempts are combined, or apply a post-hoc correction to observed scores. Using simulations calibrated to 2025 College Board data, we compare standard scoring rules against these proposed interventions.
tldr: This paper studies how retaking and aggregation policies in standardized testing affect score inflation and fairness, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper addresses fairness and accuracy in score-based admissions, but the topic is entirely outside quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a strategic framework where students allocate effort across retakes, and compare scoring policies like Superscoring and Single-Sitting using simulations calibrated to College Board data.
result: Superscoring inflates scores and amplifies wealth-based disparities, while Single-Sitting preserves signal fidelity but may exclude high-ability students lacking resources.
conclusion: Neither policy dominates; the paper proposes algorithmic interventions to balance precision and fairness, but this is unrelated to quantum information research.

title: \textsc{IH-Benchmark}: A Conflict-Centered Benchmark For Instruction-Hierarchy Robustness In Llm Applications
authors: Conor Mccauley, Zeliang Kan, Jason Martin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a language model receives conflicting instructions from different priority levels, which one does it actually follow? This question lies at the heart of reliable LLM deployment. Existing benchmarks answer this only partially, often focusing on a single hierarchy edge or adapting public datasets with limited tool-use coverage. We present IH-Benchmark, a conflict-centered benchmark for instruction-hierarchy robustness across direct system-user conflicts (S>U) and tool-mediated user-tool (U>T) conflicts. IH-Benchmark is built from a human-authored taxonomy of 44 constraint families across generic, health, finance, retail, and coding settings, and evaluates scenarios with a uniform binary pass/fail protocol combining a predicate DSL with category-scoped LLM judges. Across 37 evaluated models, hierarchy compliance ranges from 98.2% to 20.5%. We find that strong S>U compliance is not a reliable proxy for U>T robustness: several models preserve system constraints under direct user conflict but degrade sharply when conflicting instructions appear in tool outputs. Constraint hardening also reveals a split between models: some failures are largely fixed by stronger warnings, while others persist across all strictness levels. Finally, the most revealing failures are often subtle rather than overtly dangerous; models resist unauthorized purchases or bulk ticket closure more reliably than injected disclaimers or small factual distortions. These results suggest that instruction-hierarchy robustness is not a single capability, but a set of behaviors that must be evaluated across conflict surfaces, constraint types, and attack presentations.
tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating instruction-hierarchy robustness in LLMs, focusing on conflicts between system, user, and tool instructions.
motivation: Existing benchmarks for instruction hierarchy robustness are limited, often covering only single conflict types or lacking tool-use scenarios.
method: The authors construct a taxonomy of 44 constraint families across multiple domains and evaluate models using a binary pass/fail protocol with predicate DSL and LLM judges.
result: Evaluation of 37 models shows compliance ranging from 98.2% to 20.5%, revealing that system-user compliance does not predict user-tool robustness and that some failures persist despite stronger warnings.
conclusion: Instruction-hierarchy robustness is a multifaceted capability requiring evaluation across different conflict surfaces and constraint types.

title: Does Runtime Topology Context Improve LLM-Generated Kubernetes Security Patches?
authors: Farooq Shaikh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.25995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kubernetes is central to the cloud-native ecosystem, orchestrating containerised workloads. Recent work suggests that large language models (LLMs) can automate cluster security remediation, generating configuration patches from Kubernetes Security Posture Management (KSPM) findings without human authoring. Such systems, however, prompt the model with each finding in isolation from the live service call graph, assuming general hardening knowledge suffices. This assumption breaks down whenever a patch must preserve a runtime service dependency invisible to the model: an otherwise compliant fix then carries a destructive functional blast radius, crashing downstream callers or silently severing call edges across the cluster. Whether live cluster context improves patch correctness has not been measured under controlled conditions across multiple dependency classes. We introduce KuTIE (Kubernetes Topology Intelligence Engine), which builds a live cluster context from Istio call edges, Trivy KSPM findings, and the service-account bindings a workload reads, and conditions LLM patch generation on it. It is evaluated on VulnCare, a purpose-built 36-deployment, four-namespace healthcare cluster with 31 injectable findings across seven dependency classes, each labelled by topology dependence against cluster ground truth. Across 248 trials, topology context raises topology-dependent patch correctness from 11.1% to 78.0% ([MATH]), a gap that holds for every model and for six of seven classes, from credential and network-policy ([MATH]) to role-based access control ([MATH]); a topology-independent control exhibits no such effect ([MATH]), isolating the result from generic prompt enrichment. Supplying the live service-call graph and the service-account bindings it exposes thus improves remediation of topology-dependent findings well beyond scanner-only context.
tldr: This paper investigates whether providing live cluster topology context improves LLM-generated Kubernetes security patches.
motivation: Current LLM-based patch generation for Kubernetes security findings ignores runtime service dependencies, leading to patches that break cluster functionality.
method: The authors introduce KuTIE, which enriches LLM prompts with live Istio call edges, Trivy KSPM findings, and service-account bindings, and evaluate it on a purpose-built healthcare cluster with 31 findings across seven dependency classes.
result: Topology context raises topology-dependent patch correctness from 11.1% to 78.0%, with consistent improvement across models and dependency classes.
conclusion: Supplying live service-call graph and service-account bindings significantly improves remediation of topology-dependent findings beyond scanner-only context.

title: Proportional Fairness For Harmful Decisions
authors: Benjamin Cookson, Soroush Ebadian, Dominik Peters, Nisarg Shah
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study allocation of (divisible) public bads, where agents incur costs for alternatives and the goal is to pick a lottery over the alternatives. We show that the traditional definitions of the core, a central criterion of proportional representation for allocation of public goods, private goods, and private bads (chores), do not make sense for allocation of public bads. We introduce two formalizations of the core tailored to public bads. Under a structural condition which subsumes allocation of private bads, we show that zero-respecting Lindahl equilibria satisfy both formalizations, exhibit additional fairness guarantees, and strictly generalize competitive equilibria from equal incomes (CEEI) for allocation of private bads. Without this structural condition, we show that Lindahl equilibria exhibit undesirable behaviors, prove sharp impossibility results separating public bads from public goods, but show that a rule using a reduction to public goods recovers one of our formalizations of the core. Our results lay the groundwork for studying fair allocation of public bads, an overlooked yet fundamental problem, and highlight several structural and algorithmic directions that remain open.
tldr: This paper studies fair allocation of public bads using concepts from cooperative game theory and welfare economics, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The problem of fairly allocating harmful public goods (public bads) is overlooked in the fair division literature, and traditional core definitions fail for public bads.
method: The authors introduce two new core formalizations for public bads, analyze Lindahl equilibria under a structural condition, and prove impossibility results without it.
result: Zero-respecting Lindahl equilibria satisfy both core formalizations under a structural condition and generalize CEEI for private bads; without the condition, Lindahl equilibria exhibit undesirable behaviors.
conclusion: The work lays groundwork for fair allocation of public bads, highlighting structural and algorithmic open problems.

title: Freely Generated $n$-categories, Coinserters And Presentations Of Low Dimensional Categories
authors: Fernando Lucatelli Nunes
abstract: ArXiv:1704.04474v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A presentation records not only a categorical structure but also how it is assembled. This matters for rewriting, coherence, and minimality: freely adjoining a cell with prescribed boundary is different from imposing an equation between cells already constructed. We show that these two operations are governed, respectively, by coinserters and coequifiers, giving a uniform account of computadic presentations from ordinary categories to strict higher categories. For a graph [MATH], the free category on [MATH] is the coinserter in [MATH] of its domain and codomain maps between discrete categories. More generally, for every [MATH], freely adjoining [MATH]-cells with prescribed parallel boundaries to a strict [MATH]-category is a coinserter in the [MATH]-category of strict [MATH]-categories, strict [MATH]-functors, and [MATH]-icons. This construction is left adjoint to the underlying derivation-scheme functor. It recovers free strict [MATH]-categories from computads, while coequifiers impose equations between freely generated cells. In dimension two, it also satisfies a bicategorical universal property for normal pseudofunctors and icons. Replacing the walking arrow by the unit interval yields the topological coinserter of a graph. For a groupoidal [MATH]-computad [MATH], attaching one disk for each relation produces a presentation complex [MATH] whose fundamental groupoid is the groupoid presented by [MATH]. Consequently, the rank-finite deficiency of a connected groupoid is the classical deficiency of any isotropy group. Homology gives a sharp lower bound on the relations required to present a thin groupoid over a fixed graph, while crossed modules extend the comparison to relations among relations. Finally, for the descent computad, the identity and associativity confluences form a homotopy basis and attain the corresponding homological lower bounds.
tldr: This paper develops a categorical framework for freely adjoining cells and imposing equations in strict higher categories using coinserters and coequifiers.
motivation: To provide a uniform account of presentations for higher categories, clarifying the difference between freely adjoining a cell and imposing an equation.
method: Uses 2-categorical universal constructions (coinserters and coequifiers) in the category of strict n-categories, and relates them to computads and topological constructions.
result: Shows that freely adjoining n-cells is a coinserter, and coequifiers impose equations; recovers free strict n-categories from computads and gives homological bounds for groupoid presentations.
conclusion: The work offers a systematic approach to presentations of higher categories, with applications to rewriting, coherence, and homotopy theory.

title: Backpropagation For Effectful Languages I: Finite Probability And Discrete Output Algebraic Effects
authors: Diogo Simm, Fernando Lucatelli Nunes, Matthijs V\'ak\'ar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyse reverse-mode automatic differentiation (AD) for discrete probabilistic programs. Our construction is formulated in the framework of Combinatory Homomorphic Automatic Differentiation (CHAD), treating AD as a structure-preserving transformation of programs, guided by a denotational semantics. The main case study is the finite atomic distribution monad, whose computations have finite support and differentiable weights. The key point is that differentiating probabilistic programs requires cotangents to flow backwards not only through deterministic computations, but also through the probabilistic structure itself. We define the corresponding reverse-mode code transformation and prove its correctness, for handled real-output programs, by a categorical logical-relations argument. Although the paper focuses on finite discrete probability, the construction gives a reusable pattern for differentiating discrete-output algebraic effects, including finite multiset non-determinism (e.g., from fork-join parallelism), exceptions, and writer-style accumulation (e.g., for in-place accumulation of high-dimensional vectors). More broadly, we view this work as a foundational step towards extending CHAD to richer probabilistic languages and to other algebraic effects with handlers.
tldr: This paper presents a reverse-mode automatic differentiation method for discrete probabilistic programs using the CHAD framework, focusing on finite probability and algebraic effects.
motivation: To enable gradient-based learning in probabilistic programming languages with discrete distributions, which require differentiation through probabilistic structures.
method: The authors extend Combinatory Homomorphic Automatic Differentiation (CHAD) to handle the finite atomic distribution monad and other discrete-output algebraic effects, using categorical logical-relations to prove correctness.
result: They define a correct reverse-mode code transformation for discrete probabilistic programs with differentiable weights, and show the pattern generalizes to other effects like nondeterminism and exceptions.
conclusion: This work provides a foundational step for extending automatic differentiation to richer probabilistic languages and algebraic effects, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: PATHFinder Agent For Tailored Prenatal Care
authors: Vaibhav Balloli, Carissa Samuel, Samia Abdelnabi, Alex Peahl, Elizabeth Bondi-Kelly
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Prenatal care is an important preventive service designed to improve outcomes for pregnant individuals. The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) recently introduced guidelines advocating tailored prenatal care, called PATH (Plan for Tailored Healthcare). We present PATHFinder Agent(Planner for Appropriate Tailored Healthcare), an end-to-end conversational agentic system that gathers patient health and social context through structured dialogue, curates individualized prenatal care plans aligned with PATH guidelines, and surfaces community resources from Michigan 211. The system features a four-stage workflow spanning patient intake, dynamic interaction, plan synthesis, and clinician oversight. We evaluate frontier large language models (LLMs) on expert-curated rubrics across five clinical dimensions, finding that GPT-5.2 achieves the highest average score (77.6\%) while identifying key gaps in antenatal testing recommendations. We discuss future validation through human participant studies and randomized controlled trials.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent for personalized prenatal care planning based on ACOG guidelines.
motivation: To implement tailored prenatal care as recommended by new ACOG guidelines using an automated conversational agent.
method: The system uses a four-stage workflow with LLMs to gather patient context, generate care plans, and surface community resources.
result: GPT-5.2 achieved the highest average score (77.6%) on expert-curated rubrics, but gaps in antenatal testing recommendations were identified.
conclusion: The PATHFinder agent shows promise for automating prenatal care planning, but further validation through human studies is needed.

title: Stronger Memory-Query Tradeoffs For Convex Optimization: The Limitations Of Subquadratic Memory
authors: Michael Menart, Aleksandar Nikolov, Ohad Shamir
abstract: ArXiv:2607.24827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove two lower bounds for the first order oracle complexity of minimizing a [MATH]-dimensional [MATH]-Lipschitz convex function over the unit ball with [MATH] bits of memory. We first show that any such (possibly randomized) algorithm must make [MATH] oracle queries. For deterministic optimization algorithms, we show that [MATH] queries are required. For all memory regimes of interest, these improves upon the previous best known lower bounds of [MATH] and [MATH] for randomized and deterministic algorithms respectively. Notably, due to existing upper bounds, our lower bound for deterministic algorithms is the first to show a sharp oracle complexity phase transition around [MATH], where a polylogarithmic change in memory leads to a [MATH] change in the number of required oracle calls. Further, when the suboptimality is polynomially small in [MATH], our lower bound randomized algorithms is the first to show that [MATH] memory is necessary to nearly match the optimal query complexity among algorithms without memory constraints. Previously, such a result was only known for the regime where the suboptimality is quasipolynomially small in [MATH].
tldr: This paper proves lower bounds on the number of oracle queries required for convex optimization under memory constraints.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental tradeoffs between memory and query complexity in convex optimization is important for algorithm design.
method: The authors use information-theoretic arguments and adversarial constructions to derive lower bounds for both randomized and deterministic algorithms.
result: They show that any randomized algorithm requires Ω(n^2) queries and any deterministic algorithm requires Ω(n^2 log n) queries when memory is sublinear.
conclusion: The results reveal sharp phase transitions in oracle complexity as a function of memory, showing that subquadratic memory cannot achieve optimal query complexity.

motivation: Understanding how cells protect the nucleus from mechanical stress is important for cell biology and tissue mechanics.
method: The authors apply large deformations to epithelial tissues and observe the dynamics of supracellular keratin bundles and nuclear uncaging using microscopy.
result: Under large deformations, intermediate filaments bundle and ultimately release the nucleus from its cage.

motivation: Conventional microscopy cannot simultaneously achieve high resolution, large field of view, and high frame rate due to the throughput limit of optical systems.
method: The authors combine an array of 48 sensors with a diffractive mask and compressive sensing algorithms to reconstruct gigapixel-scale images at 120 fps.
result: The system achieves 25 gigapixel-per-second imaging with micrometer resolution over multi-centimeter areas.
conclusion: This approach enables real-time high-throughput microscopy for applications like biological imaging and materials inspection.

conclusion: The equilibrium lattice dynamics approach provides a predictive and efficient alternative to driven molecular dynamics for dislocation mobility in high-entropy alloys.

result: Large earthquakes tend to follow periods of high inequality in earthquake magnitudes.

result: The model demonstrates improved ability to generate consensus and manage dissent compared to traditional methods, as validated on simulated and real-world discussion data.
conclusion: Semantic-vector models offer a promising approach for enhancing collective intelligence on massive discussion platforms, with potential applications in online deliberation and decision-making.

tldr: This paper studies phototaxis in Chlamydomonas mutants lacking an eyespot, attributing directional sensitivity to cell body lensing.
motivation: Understanding how 'eyeless' mutants of Chlamydomonas still exhibit phototaxis, challenging the established role of the eyespot.
method: Theoretical modeling of light refraction through the spherical cell body, treating it as a lens, and analyzing the resulting light distribution on the photoreceptor.
result: The cell body acts as a lens, focusing light onto the photoreceptor from specific directions, explaining phototaxis sign reversal.
conclusion: Cell body lensing provides a mechanism for phototaxis in the absence of an eyespot, with implications for algal biology and bio-optics.

motivation: Understanding solute transport in microfluidic devices is important for applications like chemical analysis and drug delivery, but viscoelastic effects are not well captured by existing models.
method: The authors apply Reynolds decomposition and Taylor-Aris theory to derive a reduced-order model for the dispersion coefficient.
result: The model predicts the effective solute transport rate as a function of flow parameters and fluid rheology.
conclusion: The reduced-order model provides a computationally efficient way to predict solute dispersion in viscoelastic microchannel flows.

In this work, experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer are used to provide a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations. The results show that confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by the granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032010] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the rheology of dense vibrated granular flows, focusing on the nonmonotonic response controlled by granular temperature.
motivation: Understanding the effective viscosity of granular media under vibrations is important for industrial processes and geophysics, but a unified framework reconciling experimental observations is lacking.
method: The authors use experimentally calibrated discrete element simulations of a vane rheometer to model dense vibrated granular flows.
result: Confining pressure directly dictates the rheological response, while vibration effects are mediated by granular temperature, which results from a balance between energy input and internal dissipation.
conclusion: The study provides a unified framework that reconciles experimental observations of granular rheology under vibrations.

tldr: This paper constrains the Thomson optical depth to the CMB using Lyman-alpha forest data.
motivation: To test large values of the optical depth suggested by recent data.
method: Analysis of high-resolution Lyman-alpha forest spectra from distant QSOs.
result: Mild tension with large optical depth values, consistent with Planck satellite measurements.
conclusion: Lyman-alpha forest data support lower optical depth values, in agreement with Planck.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition, history, and recent developments of active matter, a subset of nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is often used ambiguously; the authors aim to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The paper reviews the history of the field, proposes a definition, and surveys recent topics including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.
result: A clear definition of active matter is provided, distinguishing it from other nonequilibrium systems.
conclusion: Active matter is a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems with diverse applications, but it does not directly relate to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-energy Emission From The Galactic Center
authors: Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, And Régis Terrier
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, and Régis Terrier

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. The Galactic Center also hosts diverse compact sources, plasma bubbles, and x-ray chimneys, altogether forming a dense interacting molecular zone—a gigantic powerhouse in the Milky Way.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025006] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A review of high-energy emission from the Galactic Center, covering the supermassive black hole, compact sources, and plasma bubbles.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of the high-energy phenomena in the Galactic Center region.
method: Review of observational data across multiple wavelengths, including X-ray, gamma-ray, and radio observations.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of the quiescent and flaring emission from Sgr A*, the presence of plasma bubbles and chimneys, and the interaction with the surrounding molecular zone.
conclusion: The Galactic Center is a unique laboratory for studying high-energy astrophysical processes, with many open questions remaining.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electric fields, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation and evolution.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: Recent advances provide a coherent understanding of vacuum breakdown, which can inform the design of more reliable high-power technologies and advanced accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into quantum chromodynamics, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII, highlighting recent high-precision data from BESIII.
result: The review summarizes current knowledge of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems and identifies BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: Continued experimental studies of open-charm meson pairs will advance our understanding of strong interaction dynamics and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system, focusing on observations of solar system bodies and near-Earth asteroids.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information that complements in-situ exploration, and Arecibo was the most sensitive instrument of its kind for over two decades.
method: The paper reviews the basics of planetary radar techniques and summarizes key observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: Arecibo radar observations significantly advanced our understanding of planetary surfaces and subsurface properties, and played a crucial role in characterizing near-Earth objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system left a lasting scientific legacy, and its loss underscores the need for future planetary radar capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo Observatory's contributions to radio astronomy, including pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
motivation: To document the scientific legacy of the Arecibo 305-m telescope and its upgrades over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and synthesis of key observational results from Arecibo's operations.
result: Arecibo made seminal contributions to pulsar timing, neutral hydrogen mapping, VLBI imaging, SETI, and the detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities and upgrades enabled a wide range of discoveries, cementing its place as a leading radio observatory until its collapse.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science using the Arecibo Observatory's radar, lidar, and optical instruments.
motivation: The Arecibo Observatory's unique capabilities for studying the upper atmosphere and ionosphere are highlighted.
method: The paper reviews incoherent scatter radar technique and presents results from Arecibo's suite of instruments.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are summarized.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace science, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications for understanding physical and astrophysical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star interiors and fundamental physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm rain formation is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors synthesize insights from experiments, theory, and computational models of convection-cloud chambers.
result: Convection-cloud chambers reproduce key phenomena like turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentration and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to address the precipitation bottleneck.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.

method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods in ground-based laser interferometers within multimessenger strategies.
result: The review presents the latest modeling results and signal predictions, but does not introduce new results.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a nearby supernova would significantly advance our understanding of the explosion mechanism and neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, testing the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the CMB dipole.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by examining a discrepancy between the observed matter dipole and the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in the matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, including assessment of biases and systematic effects.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard model of cosmology.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.

result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable hypothesis, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond Standard Model physics, and the HL-LHC offers a new opportunity to discover it.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels.
result: Stringent bounds have narrowed the viable parameter space, but several well-motivated scenarios remain testable at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: The HL-LHC will significantly extend the reach for supersymmetry, though discovery is not guaranteed.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and solar modeling.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive update on hydrogen-burning nuclear physics, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review discusses the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent developments in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging of optical contrast at millimeter-to-centimeter depths with high resolution, bridging the gap between optical and ultrasound imaging.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advancements in multimodal approaches enhancing its capabilities.

title: Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement And State Discrimination Measures
authors: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, And Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2174 (2026).

An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if it cannot be optimally discriminated using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the chosen discrimination measure. Specifically, we construct a family of ensembles, each consisting of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states, for which LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds in achieving optimal unambiguous discrimination. We further extend our construction to multipartite systems and provide strong numerical evidence that a similar separation between local and global optima is present for minimum-error discrimination, but not for unambiguous discrimination.
